name: ShiftBerry
whyCompetes: Offers pickup-slot signup to the same fictional coordinator.
valueProposition: Share a volunteer signup link quickly.
businessModel: Fictional free basic tier; paid reminders.
taskSteps: Create slots; send link; volunteers select slots; review roster.
taskOutcome: Slots can be filled, but overlaps are not flagged.
strength: Invented flow makes signup links easy to share.
friction: Coordinator must check overlapping shifts separately.
advantages: Fast link sharing; low initial cost.
replicability: Both appear easy to replicate in this simulation.
customerEvidence: Two invented positive comments about link sharing; one invented conflict complaint. These are not real reviews.
swotThreats: A faster conflict-safe option could displace it.
evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comments are invented

name: RosterCove
whyCompetes: Offers scheduling and overlap checks to the same fictional coordinator.
valueProposition: Plan recurring volunteer shifts with conflict warnings.
taskEntry: Coordinator creates an account and recurring schedule.
taskSteps: Set recurrence; import availability; assign people; resolve flagged overlap; publish.
taskOutcome: Overlapping assignments are flagged before publication.
strength: Invented flow catches the target error.
friction: Several setup screens and an account for a small event.
replicability: Conflict logic appears replicable; recurring workflow takes more work.
customerEvidence: Two invented positive comments about warnings; one invented setup complaint. These are not real reviews.
swotThreats: A lighter tool with the same warning could displace it.
evidenceType: Observed in synthetic fixture; reported comments are invented

name: PatchPad
whyCompetes: A generic shared table can hold the same three pickup slots.
valueProposition: Let a small group edit a shared table.
taskSteps: Make rows; share edit access; volunteers add names; manually inspect conflicts.
taskOutcome: Assignments are visible; overlap checking is manual.
strength: Flexible, low-effort setup in the invented flow.
replicability: Generic table is easy to imitate but its familiarity may be hard to displace.
customerEvidence: One invented positive comment only; it is an anecdote, not a pattern.
swotThreats: Purpose-built tools could reduce coordinator effort.

name: Paper board
whyCompetes: A coordinator can fill slots by asking volunteers on site.
valueProposition: List available shifts without a device or account.
businessModel: No software charge; coordinator time is required.
taskEntry: Coordinator posts a board at the swap.
taskSteps: Write slots; collect names; remember or manually verify conflicts.
taskOutcome: On-site names are recorded; remote volunteers cannot see current assignments.
friction: Remote visibility and conflict checking are weak.
advantages: Zero software cost; visible on site.
replicability: Trivial to copy; no durable technical advantage.
customerEvidence: One invented missed-shift comment only; it is an anecdote, not a pattern.
swotWeaknesses: No remote access or automatic warning.
swotOpportunities: Could combine with a phone photo or message.
